# Run a live television desk in the On Air at Eight showcase

## Visitor outcome
Run the opening of a live TV show. A remote guest is late and a ninety-second film is ready. Changing the rundown should change the presenter’s next cue and what the audience sees at the end of the titles. This is a playable example for the examples overview in #21140.

## Delivery
Use a store-backed Neo rundown with pointer ordering, an accessible alternative, a visible program feed and presenter cues. Give the presenter a second-window view when supported. Use local, authored visuals and a replayable show clock. Existing precedents include `examples/list/reorder`, `examples/dashboard/tearOut` and Workstation Planning #21223.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A first-time visitor understands the deadline, unavailable guest and ready film from the opening screen.
- [ ] Dragging the film ahead of the interview changes the next cue. Taking the broadcast produces the corresponding picture. Leaving the original order produces visible dead air.
- [ ] Replay restores the opening and an equivalent keyboard path plays the rescue.
- [ ] The presenter view follows the same director’s changes in a real popup. One screen remains sufficient to play.
- [ ] The examples catalog opens the showcase and uses its actual picture. A headless browser exercises the interactions.

## Scope and prior art
One simulated broadcast. No external stream or account. The generic desktop window tear-out work keeps its own scope in #21603. Checked latest 20 open issues, open/closed broadcast and rundown search, own assignments, recent A2A claims, KB and Memory Core on November 20. No existing broadcast-showcase owner found. Open issue count at sweep: 83.
